current_activity: Alpine front: the division liberates Briancon and Modane
notes: Event date: 14 October 1944 (Wikipedia). Event definition: Landed in southern France at the end of August 1944, the division is moved to the Alpine front, where it liberates Briancon and Modane on 14 October. Event support: one source family (Wikipedia). Wikipedia, 2nd Moroccan Infantry Division, section French & German campaign (1944-1945): "There, it liberated Briançon and Modane on October 14". Location: Briançon, Hautes-Alpes (new place) with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: the point is Briancon; Modane is about 50 km to the north. Location support: Wikipedia names Briancon and Modane, about 50 km apart; the point is Briancon, precision 10 km. Commander: General Marcel Carpentier commands the division, September 1944 to April 1945 (Wikipedia).

source_locator: R053: section French & German campaign (1944-1945); R651: p. 419; R686: pp. 243-246
current_activity: Belfort Gap offensive: the division pierces the German position and enters Belfort
notes: Event date: 25 November 1944 (Wikipedia; CMH Riviera to the Rhine, p. 419). Event definition: Under General Carpentier the division pierces the German position in the Belfort Gap on 14 November, seizes Montbeliard and Hericourt and enters Belfort on 25 November, with combat command CC6 of the 5th Armored Division attached. Event support: two source families (Wikipedia and the US Army official history (CMH)), and de Lattre's History of the French First Army, which disagrees on the date. Wikipedia, 2nd Moroccan Infantry Division, section French & German campaign (1944-1945): "it was positioned opposite the Belfort gap, pierced the German position on November 14, seized Montbéliard and Héricourt, and entered Belfort on November 25"; CMH Riviera to the Rhine ch. 23 p. 419: "In fact, the 2d Moroccan Division, even with the support of CC6, was unable to clear the Belfort area until 25 November"; de Lattre, The History of the French First Army (1952) p. 243-246: "They only surrendered on the 21st, when Belfort had fallen.". Location: Belfort, Territoire de Belfort with a precision of 5 km. Location support: Wikipedia names Belfort and the CMH history the Belfort area, both for 25 November and the division: two source families for an area-level place, so 0.7. French follow-up: confidence raised from 0.5 to 0.7 after the CMH history (p. 419) was read as a second source family. Commander: General Marcel Carpentier commands the division, September 1944 to April 1945 (Wikipedia). Review (French follow-up, de Lattre): de Lattre (pp. 243-246), in the pages on the 2nd DIM (8th and 4th RTM) in the Belfort woods and forts, says the forts surrendered on 21 November "when Belfort had fallen", four days before the 25 November of Wikipedia and the CMH history (which says the division could not clear the Belfort area until 25 November). The two can be read as the town (21 November) and the whole area (25 November); not reconciled, so the row keeps 25 November and 0.7.

current_activity: Assault crossing of the Rhine at Germersheim
notes: Event date: 31 March 1945 (CMH The Last Offensive, p. 322; Wikipedia). Event definition: The division makes the second French assault crossing of the Rhine at Germersheim on 31 March, a more conventional crossing than at Speyer that fares less well at first. Event support: two source families (the US Army official history (CMH) and Wikipedia). CMH The Last Offensive ch. 15 p. 322: "A few miles upstream at Germersheim, a more conventional crossing fared less well. Because of confusion at hastily chosen embarkation points, the first wave of the 2d Moroccan Division"; Wikipedia, 2nd Moroccan Infantry Division, section French & German campaign (1944-1945): "crossed the Rhine on March 31, 1945". Location: Germersheim, Rheinland-Pfalz with a precision of 3 km. Location support: the CMH history places the crossing at Germersheim and Wikipedia dates it; two source families. Commander: General Marcel Carpentier commands the division, September 1944 to April 1945 (Wikipedia).

current_activity: Enters Karlsruhe; the CMH history dates the capture of the city to 4 April
notes: Event date: 3 April 1945 (Wikipedia); the CMH history gives 4 April for the capture (The Last Offensive, p. 427). Event definition: From the Rhine bridgehead the division enters Karlsruhe on 3 April (Wikipedia); the CMH history dates the French capture of the city to 4 April without naming the division. Event support: two source families (Wikipedia and the US Army official history (CMH)). Wikipedia, 2nd Moroccan Infantry Division, section French & German campaign (1944-1945): "It entered Karlsruhe on April 3, Pforzheim on April 8"; CMH The Last Offensive ch. 18 p. 427: "Having quickly captured Karlsruhe (4 April) and Pforzheim (8 April)". Location: Karlsruhe, Baden-Württemberg (new place) with a precision of 5 km. Location support: Wikipedia names Karlsruhe for the division; the CMH history does not name the division, so one source family for the unit.
